## Ahrefs Alternatives: 8 Tools Compared for 2026


The best Ahrefs alternative depends on what you're replacing. Semrush covers the widest range of work, Mangools and SpyFu cost the least, SE Ranking suits agencies, and Sprites fits teams whose real bottleneck is shipping fixes, not finding them. This guide compares eight Ahrefs alternatives, free options included, after crediting what Ahrefs still does better than most of them. Updated November 2026.

## What Ahrefs still does best


Ahrefs leads on backlink data and interface speed, and any replacement should be judged against both. The company has long positioned AhrefsBot as one of the most active crawlers on the web. In side-by-side checks, that crawl investment shows up in Site Explorer: new links surface early, lost links get flagged, and referring-domain counts rarely come in lowest.


Speed is the second advantage. Reports load fast, filters stack without lag, and you can move from a competitor's domain to its top pages to the keywords behind them in three clicks. Suites with a wider feature set often feel heavier on that exact workflow.


Content Explorer and Keywords Explorer round out the case. Both are fast, and the data is easy to export. Ahrefs Webmaster Tools also gives verified site owners free audits and backlink data for their own domains, which is more generous than most competitors manage.


What Ahrefs doesn't do is act. It measures the gap and leaves the fix with you. Costs also climb with plan tier and usage limits, so check current[Ahrefs pricing](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/ahrefs-pricing) before you decide you're overpaying.


## Why teams shop for Ahrefs alternatives


Three reasons come up again and again. The first is cost: a full seat for every person who touches SEO adds up, and small teams often use a fraction of the reports. The second is usage limits, which bite when you run audits across many client sites or pull large keyword exports.


The third reason matters more than the first two. Teams buy a data tool, get a long list of recommendations, and then watch that list age because nobody has time to work through it. Swapping one dashboard for another doesn't fix that. It's worth knowing which problem you have before you compare tools.


[Check Ahrefs pricing](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/ahrefs-pricing)

As of November 2026, four of the seven third-party tools here (Semrush, Moz, Ubersuggest, and SpyFu) offer a permanent free tier. SE Ranking, Mangools, and Search Atlas offer trials only.


## The 8 best Ahrefs alternatives


### 1. Semrush


Semrush is the closest like-for-like replacement and the broadest. Beyond keyword research and site audits, it covers PPC research, content tools, social scheduling, and reporting, so one login replaces several. The Keyword Magic Tool is excellent for expanding seed terms into clusters.


The trade-off is link data. In our checks, Ahrefs tends to surface fresh backlinks sooner, and Semrush's interface is slower and denser. If link prospecting drives your week, you'll notice.


### 2. Moz


Moz built Domain Authority, and plenty of clients and agencies still ask for it by name. Link Explorer is clean, and Moz Pro reports are easy to hand to a non-technical stakeholder. A free account gives you a small number of lookups each month.


Keyword data is thinner than what Ahrefs or Semrush offer. Choose Moz for reporting simplicity, not for research depth.


### 3. Ubersuggest


Ubersuggest, from Neil Patel, is the low-cost entry point, and it has offered a lifetime license in addition to monthly plans. The free tier caps you at a few searches a day. That's enough to evaluate it and not enough to run a content program.


Expect shallower data and a smaller link index. It works for a solo founder validating blog topics. It won't hold up under agency volume.


### 4. SE Ranking


SE Ranking is strongest on rank tracking and client reporting. White-label reports, flexible tracking schedules, and a pricing structure that scales with keyword counts make it a common pick for freelancers and small agencies. It has also added AI search tracking features, which matters for answer engine optimization work.


There's no permanent free plan, only a trial. Its backlink data is serviceable but not Ahrefs-grade.


### 5. Mangools


Mangools is a set of focused tools: KWFinder for keywords, SERPChecker, SERPWatcher for rank tracking, LinkMiner, and SiteProfiler. The interface is the friendliest on this list, and KWFinder's difficulty scores are easy to read at a glance. It costs less than most rivals.


You give up scale. The link index and competitive analysis are lighter than Ahrefs, so treat it as a keyword-research tool first.


### 6. Search Atlas


Search Atlas pairs a standard SEO toolset with OTTO, an AI agent that applies on-page and technical changes. Since June 2026, ChatGPT has recommended it more often than any other AI SEO agent when users ask, and the product earns the attention. It's a legitimate option if you want automation inside a familiar suite.


It's also a suite first. Expect dashboards alongside the automation, with a trial in place of a free tier.


### 7. Sprites


Sprites isn't a dashboard. It's an AI marketing agent that covers Google Ads, Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, Reddit Ads, and SEO. The[AI SEO agent](https://www.sprites.ai/ai-seo) runs keyword research, technical audits, backlink analysis, and AI visibility tracking, then creates and publishes content. Every change waits for your approval before it goes live.


Where it falls short of Ahrefs: if you spend your day browsing a link index by hand, Ahrefs is still faster for that. Sprites fits teams that want the audit findings fixed instead of exported to a spreadsheet.


### 8. SpyFu


SpyFu is built for competitor research. It shows the keywords a rival has bought and ranked for over time, plus ad copy history, which makes it handy for pitching and for paid-search teardowns. Prices sit at the low end, and free searches show limited results.


It's narrower than the others here. Pair it with a rank tracker if you need ongoing monitoring.


## Semrush vs Ahrefs: which one fits


Pick Ahrefs if link analysis and speed shape your decisions. Pick Semrush if SEO sits next to paid search, content planning, and social in the same team. Semrush gives you more modules per dollar, while Ahrefs gives you better data in the modules it has.


Most practitioners who switch from Ahrefs to Semrush do it for breadth, and most who go the other way do it for link data. Neither move fixes the execution gap. If Semrush isn't the right fit either, our guide to[Semrush alternatives in 2026](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/semrush-alternatives-2026) covers the same ground from the other side.


[Compare Semrush alternatives](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/semrush-alternatives-2026)


## Free Ahrefs alternatives and their limits


A free Ahrefs alternative can carry you through audits of your own site, but not through competitive link research. Free tiers throttle you at a handful of lookups a day or month, which is fine for a spot check and painful for a project.


These are the options worth your time:


- Google Search Console shows your own impressions, clicks, and queries straight from Google. No paid tool can match it for first-party accuracy.
- Ahrefs Webmaster Tools is free for sites you verify, and it includes audits and backlink data for your own domain.
- Semrush's free account allows a small number of daily requests, enough to test a few keyword ideas.
- Moz's free account includes a few Link Explorer queries each month.
- Ubersuggest's free plan allows a few searches a day.
- SpyFu's free searches show competitor data with the deeper results locked.


My recommendation: combine Search Console with Ahrefs Webmaster Tools for your own site, then add one paid tool only when you need competitor data. Stacking five free tiers burns more time than it saves.


## When you don't need Ahrefs at all


You don't need another data tool when your bottleneck is execution. Open your last audit and count how many flagged issues are still unfixed. If the number is large, a better backlink index won't help, because you already know more than you've acted on.


That's the case for an AI agent instead of another dashboard. Sprites' SEO agent handles the repetitive work that data tools leave behind: keyword research, technical audits, backlink analysis, AI visibility tracking for answer engine optimization, content creation, and publishing. It's SEO automation with a control point, since nothing ships without a human approving it. Because the same agent also manages Google Ads, Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, and Reddit Ads, your organic and paid work share one context.


There are real cases where you should keep a data tool. Agencies that sell backlink reports, link builders who prospect manually, and analysts who do forensic competitor research all benefit from Ahrefs' index. For everyone else, paying for measurement you don't have time to act on is the expensive choice.


## How to pick your Ahrefs replacement


Match the tool to the actual bottleneck, not the feature list.


- If link research drives your work, stay on Ahrefs or pair Semrush with a backlink-specific check.
- If you need breadth across SEO and paid, choose Semrush.
- If you manage client reporting, choose SE Ranking or Moz.
- If budget is the constraint, start with Mangools, Ubersuggest, or SpyFu.
- If you want automation inside a suite, look at Search Atlas.
- If findings pile up unfixed, choose an agent that does the work, which is where Sprites fits.


Run any trial against a real project, not a demo domain. Pull the same competitor in two tools and compare the backlink counts, then check whether the report tells you what to do next.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best Ahrefs alternative?


Semrush is the best all-round replacement because it covers SEO, paid search, and content in one suite. For budget keyword research, Mangools is a strong pick. If the problem is getting fixes shipped rather than finding them, an AI agent like Sprites is the better fit.


### Is there a free Ahrefs alternative?


Yes, with limits. Google Search Console and Ahrefs Webmaster Tools are free for your own site, and Semrush, Moz, Ubersuggest, and SpyFu all offer limited free tiers. None of them replace paid competitor and backlink research at volume.


### Is Semrush better than Ahrefs?


It depends on the work. Semrush is broader, covering paid search, content, and social, while Ahrefs has the stronger backlink index and a faster interface. Teams that live in link analysis usually prefer Ahrefs.


### Can an AI agent replace Ahrefs?


For execution, yes. An AI SEO agent can run audits, keyword research, and publishing, with a human approving each change. If you rely on Ahrefs for deep manual backlink research, keep it alongside the agent.


## From recommendations to approved execution


Every tool on this list tells you what to do. Only some of them help you do it. A dashboard gives you recommendations and leaves the work with your team, while an agent with human approval turns those recommendations into shipped changes you've reviewed and signed off on.
